_doc: Category 25 (Cannabis, Hemp, and CBD Products) HMTc standard compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit default, ROUTE-PRESERVING. For each (subcategory, analyte) the config names EXPLICITLY the applicable sovereign cannabis maximums as a set of register-row ids; the compiler takes the strictest (min) as the HMTc value (a lookup, never an occurrence percentile). The applicable pool for a row is the route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules (MA all-uses, Nevada, Israel) plus that row's own route-specific rules (California inhalable/non-inhalable, Colorado inhaled/oral/topical, Maryland inhalation/oral/cutaneous/edible, MA ingestion-only). An inhalation-route limit is NEVER applied to an ingested or topical product, and vice-versa; where a stricter cannabis limit exists but belongs to a different route it is listed in audit_excluded_ids with a documented reason and the compiler's verify pass confirms every stricter-unselected cannabis row is either applied or so acknowledged. Vape hardware is intentionally NOT compiled: its governing quantity is metal RELEASE into inhaled aerosol, not total product content, and the aerosol-release test architecture is a reserved governance decision (see reserved below and docs/governance/category-25-step0-lock.md). Numeric outputs are STAFF/HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, route-preserving; strictest applicable sovereign cannabis maximum; occurrence never selects a value)

iAs.control: Cannabis programs set arsenic limits without speciation; these are recorded and certified as total arsenic. Total As is measured on every lot and bounds the inorganic fraction; any elevated total-As result triggers iAs speciation.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS on an elevated total-As result.

MeHg.control: Cannabis has no methylmercury bioaccumulation pathway. Total Hg is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction; there is no route by which a certified cannabis product accumulates MeHg above the total-Hg limit.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation only on an anomalous total-Hg result.

Ni.control: Nickel is a mandatory total-panel result because cannabis accumulates Ni from soil and inhalation hardware can release it, but no loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a finished-product total-Ni maximum. Report every result, investigate source and route, and do not represent this cell as a numeric government limit.
Ni.reference_method: Total Ni by ICP-MS; for inhaled products, aerosol-emissions testing separates plant/extract contamination from hardware release.

Sn.control: No loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a total-tin maximum. Total Sn remains mandatory surveillance, with any quantifiable result investigated for packaging, solder, catalyst, or device contact.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; organotin speciation when the formulation, elastomer, catalyst, or packaging pathway makes organotin plausible.

Al.control: No loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a total-aluminium maximum. Total Al remains mandatory surveillance and elevated results trigger soil, processing-aid, excipient, or device-source investigation.
Al.reference_method: Total Al by ICP-MS with route-appropriate blank and device controls.

Cr-VI.control: Total chromium is measured on every lot. Inhaled products and any anomalous total-Cr result require Cr(VI) speciation; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by validated species-specific IC-ICP-MS with matrix-specific recovery controls.

cannabis-vape-hardware.name: Vape hardware and aerosol emissions
cannabis-vape-hardware.reason: The consumable (cartridge fill / vape oil) is compiled separately on the inhaled-route total-content basis (see subcategory cannabis-vape-cartridge-fill). What remains reserved is metal RELEASE from the device heating element into the inhaled aerosol (coil leaching of Pb, Ni, and Cr) and the aerosol-emission behaviour of the heated oil — a different measured quantity (mass emitted, not total content). A ug/kg product-content limit cannot express it. The aerosol-emissions test architecture — and whether hardware is factored per-category here or under one shared inhalable-hardware treatment with nicotine vapes — is a reserved governance decision for Karen (docs/governance/taxonomy-reorganization-2026-06.md section 4; category-25-step0-lock.md). No emissions standard is set until that architecture is locked.
cannabis-vape-hardware.governing_basis_when_unreserved: aerosol-emissions basis (mass emitted per puff or per gram aerosolized), not product-content ug/kg; Pb/Ni/Cr released from the heating element are the primary analytes.

The binding health control is Cr(VI): any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
